title: Local Numerical Superiority
content: Creating a local numerical overload in a specific zone (more attackers than defenders there) is the foundation of nearly all successful attacking play. A 3v2 in a zone near the penalty area, a 2v1 on the flank, or a 4v3 in central midfield — each forces a defender to make an impossible choice: cover two players simultaneously or concede one free. The overload is created by rotations, third-man movements, and positional play bringing players into the key zone before the ball arrives. Important distinction: numerical overload does not mean crowding into a small area — the overload should be in a zone with enough space that superior numbers can be used effectively. Three players in 5m radius are easy to block; three players in 20m radius with movement creates a genuine dilemma.
